newsitem.title: USA: USDA has no comment on Brazil coffee figures.
newsitem.headline: USDA has no comment on Brazil coffee figures.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it had no comment on conflicting Brazil coffee crop forecasts that have prompted concern by the Association of Coffee Producing Countries.
"I wouldn't call that a discrepancy," said Frank Hokana, a coffee expert with the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service, referring to a 4-million bag difference in the figures.
"I have no comment," he said. "We do plan to respond to the inquiries that have been made."
Tuesday, USDA made public an agricultural attache report dated May 12 which estimated Brazil's 1997/98 harvest at 24 million bags of coffee. On June 13, USDA issued an estimate of 28 million bags.
While attache reports are not considered official USDA data, they are considered key indicators of how the agency calculates and prepares its final estimates.
Association of Coffee Producing Countries said earlier Wednesday it would seek an explanation from USDA.
